common.proposalNotice: This is a proposal prototype, not an official system adopted by the General Authority of Civil Aviation.

landing.heroTitle: Your self-built drone deserves a legal registration
landing.heroSubtitle: Registration today requires a manufacturer serial number. Self-built and FPV aircraft don't have one, so they stay outside the system. Ajniha replaces the serial number with Remote ID.
landing.gapBody: There is currently no lawful path for a self-built drone operator. No registration, and nowhere sanctioned to fly.
landing.remoteIdTitle: Remote ID instead of a serial number
landing.remoteIdBody: Remote ID is the direction regulation is already moving. Ajniha issues each aircraft a unique identifier that a field inspector can scan.
landing.accountabilityBody: A field inspector scans the code and sees that the aircraft is registered and accountable — without seeing who owns it. Revealing identity is a restricted permission, and every reveal is logged.

rule.title: Registration asks for a serial number
rule.body: Drone registration today rests on a manufacturer's serial number, treated as the airframe's permanent identity.

gap.title: Some aircraft have none
gap.body: A self-built or FPV aircraft is assembled from parts. There is no manufacturer, no serial number, and no field that can honestly be filled in.

consequence.title: So there is nowhere to register, and nowhere to fly
consequence.body: A pilot who cannot register cannot book, and has no sanctioned airspace. The aircraft does not disappear — it flies outside the system.

landing.cardQrAlt: QR code for an example Remote ID card
landing.cardScanHint: Scan it: you reach the same public verification page a field inspector does. This code is reserved for demonstration and belongs to no registered aircraft.
landing.mapBody: The city is restricted by default, with specific permitted areas carved out inside it and absolute no-fly zones layered on top. Flying starts with booking an area, not with take-off.
landing.mapAlt: Diagram of the airspace zones over Riyadh

register.title: Register the aircraft
register.body: Enter the airframe's specifications and photographs. For a self-built drone, the serial number field is not shown at all.

remoteId.title: Receive your Remote ID
remoteId.body: Once approved, your aircraft is issued a Remote ID and a QR code to print and fix to the airframe.

book.title: Book an area and a time
book.body: Choose a permitted area and a slot. The platform checks altitude, weight and operating hours before it approves.

fly.title: Fly within the booking
fly.body: Anyone who scans your aircraft sees a valid registration and an authorised flight — without seeing who you are.

landing.forGacaBody: The oversight side of the same system: decisions on the record, a log with no edit path, and a field verification tool.

queues.title: Review queues
queues.body: Registrations reach a human reviewer who approves, or refuses with a written reason the owner can read.

compliance.title: Compliance indicators
compliance.body: Registration, booking and report volumes, and rejection rates with their reasons.

lookup.title: Field verification
lookup.body: Scanning an aircraft's code returns its registration status at once. Revealing the owner is a restricted power, and every reveal is recorded.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Every decision and every identity reveal is written to a log the product has no path to edit or delete.

landing.footerLine: Ajniha — a proposed platform for drone registration and airspace booking.

howItWorks.pageLead: From creating an account to taking off — and what a stranger sees when they scan your aircraft. This is the whole path, as a pilot meets it.

account.title: Create your account and complete your profile
account.body: The account is yours, not the aircraft's. You give your name, your contact details and your national ID or Iqama number once, and they carry across every aircraft you register afterwards.
account.detail: A reviewer checks your identity. There is no automated verification and no SMS — a person reads the document and decides.

register.title: Register the aircraft, serial number or not
register.body: You describe the aircraft: build type, weight class, manufacturer and model if it has them, and photographs. The serial number field is optional.
register.detail: This is the entire point. A self-built or FPV aircraft has no serial number, and that does not stop it being registered here.

review.title: A person reviews it
review.body: The registration sits under review until a reviewer opens it, and is then either approved or rejected with a written reason you can read.
review.detail: A rejection is not the end of it: you fix what was asked for and resubmit. Every decision is written to the audit trail under the name of whoever made it.

identity.title: Your Remote ID and QR code are issued
identity.body: On approval the aircraft gets its own Remote ID code, a digital card, and a QR code you can print and fix to the airframe.
identity.detail: The code stays the same for the life of the aircraft, renewal included, so a printed sticker never dies.

book.title: Book a zone and a slot
book.body: You pick a permitted zone and a slot inside its opening hours. The system checks the zone, the ceiling, the weight class, the build type and any temporary closure before it answers.
book.detail: A refusal comes back as specific reasons rather than a generic message, so you know exactly which rule stopped you.

renew.title: Fly, then renew
renew.body: You fly inside the zone you booked and within its window. The registration has a validity period, and you are told before it lapses.
renew.detail: Once it has lapsed the code still scans — it simply reports that the registration has expired instead of that it is valid.

howItWorks.refusalsLead: Everything is closed by default. Better to know that before you drive out to the site.

outside.title: Outside a permitted zone
outside.body: The launch point is inside the Riyadh area but not inside any published permitted zone.

closed.title: Outside opening hours, or during a closure
closed.body: Each zone has two windows a day, and Friday is split around Jumu'ah. A temporary closure overrides the published hours.

ceiling.title: Above the ceiling
ceiling.body: Each zone has a ceiling in metres above ground level. It is not advisory.

capacity.title: The zone is full
capacity.body: Each slot has a limited number of seats. Two bookings for the same place at the same time cannot both succeed.

status.title: The aircraft is not approved
status.body: A draft, a registration still under review, and a revoked or expired one: none of them can book.

howItWorks.privacyLead: Anyone who scans your aircraft sees the registration status, the build type, the weight class and the city of registration. They do not see your name, your mobile number, your ID number, or where you are flying. An authorised reviewer can reveal the owner when they need to — after writing a reason, and the reveal is recorded against their name.
howItWorks.nextBody: Registering here does not need a serial number.

remoteIdPage.pageLead: A digital licence plate for drones: an identifier broadcast during flight that ties what you can see in the sky to a record someone can look up. This page explains the two models the rule rests on — the American one and the Saudi one — and why an Ajniha Remote ID is a workable substitute for a serial number.
remoteIdPage.whatBody: It is not tracking and it is not a camera. It is a short message broadcast from the aircraft while it flies, carrying an identifier, a position, an altitude, a speed and the pilot's location, and any device nearby can receive it.
remoteIdPage.whatBody2: The identifier by itself says nothing about the owner. Its value is that it points at a record: whoever is authorised to look that record up learns who the aircraft belongs to, and everyone else sees a number. That separation between identifier and identity is what makes the model workable at all.
remoteIdPage.faaBody: The FAA's Remote ID rule is Part 89 of Title 14, and it offers three ways to comply.

standard.title: An aircraft that broadcasts by itself
standard.body: An aircraft built to broadcast its own identity.

module.title: A fitted broadcast module
module.body: A part fixed to an aircraft that does not broadcast, which broadcasts on its behalf. This is the route open to home-built aircraft.

fria.title: A recognized area where you may fly without broadcasting
fria.body: A specific site where flight without broadcast is allowed, provided the aircraft stays within visual line of sight.

remoteIdPage.faaIdentityBody: What matters in the rule is that the identity being broadcast is not necessarily the aircraft's serial number. The text offers a choice:
remoteIdPage.faaModuleBody: And with a fitted module, the number broadcast is the module's own serial number, not that of the aircraft carrying it:
remoteIdPage.gacaTitle: The Saudi model: Direct or Network Remote ID
remoteIdPage.gacaBody: Subpart F of GACAR Part 107 carries an explicit application date, and requires every registered aircraft — model aircraft included — to carry one of two systems.
remoteIdPage.gacaDriBody: Direct Remote ID (DRI) broadcasts the operator's registration number and the verification code GACA issued, then the serial number of the fitted add-on:
remoteIdPage.gacaNriBody: Network Remote ID (NRI), by contrast, also requires the aircraft's own serial number — and that is the practical difference between the two routes:
remoteIdPage.gacaVersionNote: The passages above are quoted from Version 4.0 of Part 107, which is the edition that could be obtained. GACA's own log of versions shows the current edition is 5.0, and that its amendments concern standard scenarios and pilot training rather than Subpart F.
remoteIdPage.gapBody: The common belief is that registration requires a manufacturer's serial number. GACA's own documents are more careful than that: the serial is essential information for the Specific Category only, is asked for in the Open Category if it is available, and the identifier an aircraft displays may be the registration certificate number instead.
remoteIdPage.gapBody2: So the gap is not the serial number. It is what the identifier points at: a home-built aircraft has no number and no record tying it to an accountable person, so there is nothing to look up when somebody sees it overhead.
remoteIdPage.gapBody3: From 1 January 2026 this gets sharper still: what has to be broadcast is a registration number issued by an authority, not a factory marking. And whoever issues the number holds the record. That is exactly what Ajniha does.
remoteIdPage.ajnihaBody: A Remote ID issued by the platform, bound to a registered aircraft and to an owner whose identity a person has checked.

code.title: A stable code
code.body: One code for the life of the aircraft, in a form you can read out and say aloud, and it survives renewal.

record.title: A record behind it
record.body: The code points at an approved registration: build type, weight class, city of registration, and an accountable owner.

scan.title: A public page when it is scanned
scan.body: Anyone who scans the code reaches a page stating the registration's status, with nothing about the owner on it.

reveal.title: A reveal that is logged, never automatic
reveal.body: An authorised reviewer can reveal the owner after writing a reason, and the reveal is written to the audit trail before anything is shown.

renewal.title: A sticker that does not die
renewal.body: Renewal does not change the code, because the sticker may have been on the airframe for years.

remoteIdPage.notBody: This is said plainly, because the rest of the page means nothing without it.

notRadio.title: Not a radio
notRadio.body: An Ajniha code is an identifier in a register, not a signal transmitted from the aircraft, and it does not replace a DRI or NRI unit.

notCertified.title: Not a certified system
notCertified.body: The platform has not been evaluated or accepted as a Direct or Network Remote ID system under any regulation.

notGaca.title: Not issued by GACA
notGaca.body: Ajniha is an independent proposal. Nothing here implies that the General Authority of Civil Aviation has approved or adopted it.

notLegal.title: It does not make your flight lawful
notLegal.body: If your aircraft carries a real broadcast module, declare it here for a reviewer to check. The regulation, not this page, remains the authority.

fixes.outside_permitted_zone: Pick a point inside a permitted zone on the map.
fixes.inside_restricted_zone: Choose a permitted zone, or request an exception review.
fixes.inside_no_fly_zone: There is no exception here. Choose another zone.
fixes.above_ceiling: Reduce your altitude to {ceiling} m or below.
fixes.below_floor: Raise your altitude to {floor} m or above.
fixes.zone_suspended: Watch for the zone reopening, or choose an alternative.
fixes.zone_closed_window: Choose a window outside the closure.
fixes.night_operation_not_permitted: Choose a window between sunrise and sunset.
fixes.slot_full: Pick one of the alternative slots.
fixes.slot_not_on_grid: Choose a slot from the grid shown.
fixes.booking_lead_time: Choose a window more than {hours} hours from now.
fixes.duplicate_booking: Cancel the existing booking or choose a different window.
fixes.no_remote_id: Complete registration to have a Remote ID issued.
fixes.remote_id_not_active: Renew the registration to reactivate the Remote ID.
fixes.broadcast_rid_required: Use an aircraft that broadcasts Direct Remote ID.
fixes.build_type_not_permitted: Choose a zone that allows this build type.
fixes.weight_class_not_permitted: Choose a zone that allows this class, or a lighter aircraft.
fixes.pilot_profile_incomplete: Complete your details and identity document.
fixes.identity_unverified: Wait for your identity document to be reviewed. We'll let you know.
fixes.rate_limited: Wait a moment and try again.

meta.description: A proposed platform for registering self-built drones using Remote ID, and booking flight slots in designated zones.

dashboard.title: My dashboard
dashboard.noUpcoming: You have no approved flights coming up.
dashboard.onboardingIntro: Three steps between you and a legal flight.

actions.completeProfile: Your pilot profile is not complete.
actions.awaitingVerification: Your identity document is waiting to be reviewed.

onboardingHint.profile: Your name, your ID document, and how to reach you.
onboardingHint.drone: Self-built and FPV aircraft are welcome — no serial number needed.

verifyEmail.subject: Confirm your email address
verifyEmail.preview: Finish setting up your Ajniha account
verifyEmail.heading: Confirm your email address
verifyEmail.body: An Ajniha account was created with this email address. Confirm it to activate the account.
verifyEmail.ignore: If you didn't create this account, ignore this message and nothing will happen.

resetPassword.subject: Reset your password
resetPassword.preview: A link to reset your account password
resetPassword.heading: Reset your password
resetPassword.body: We received a request to reset the password on your Ajniha account.
resetPassword.expiry: This link is valid for {minutes} minutes from when it was sent.
resetPassword.ignore: If you didn't ask for this, ignore the message — your password hasn't changed.

droneApproved.subject: {nickname} is registered
droneApproved.heading: Registration approved
droneApproved.body: “{nickname}” is registered. The code below is its Remote ID — what identifies it in place of a manufacturer serial number.
droneApproved.keepCode: Print the QR code from the card and fix it to the airframe. The same code survives renewal, so you won't need a new sticker.

droneRejected.subject: {nickname} needs a change before it can be registered
droneRejected.preview: A reviewer asked for a change before approval
droneRejected.heading: Not approved yet
droneRejected.body: A reviewer looked at the registration for “{nickname}” and couldn't approve it as submitted.
droneRejected.whatNext: Fix what's described above and resubmit the same request. You don't need to start a new registration.

droneExpiring.subject: {nickname}'s registration is running out
droneExpiring.preview: Renew before it lapses to keep booking flights
droneExpiring.heading: “{nickname}”'s registration is running out
droneExpiring.body: Once the registration lapses, you won't be able to book flight slots with this aircraft.
droneExpiring.remaining: {days, plural, =0 {Expires today} one {1 day} other {# days}}
droneExpiring.keepsCode: Renewing keeps the same Remote ID code, so the sticker already on the airframe stays valid.

droneExpired.subject: {nickname}'s registration has lapsed
droneExpired.preview: Booking flights with this aircraft is blocked until you renew
droneExpired.heading: “{nickname}”'s registration has lapsed
droneExpired.body: This aircraft's registration is no longer valid.
droneExpired.blocked: Flight slots can't be booked with an aircraft whose registration has lapsed.
droneExpired.keepsCode: Renewing keeps the same Remote ID code, so the sticker already on the airframe stays valid.

bookingApproved.subject: Your booking at {zone} is approved
bookingApproved.preview: The details of your approved flight slot
bookingApproved.heading: Booking approved
bookingApproved.body: The flight slot below is approved.
bookingApproved.note: The approval covers this slot and this zone only. Any change of time or place needs a new booking.

bookingRejected.subject: Your booking at {zone} wasn't approved
bookingRejected.preview: Why it wasn't approved, and other slots
bookingRejected.heading: Booking not approved
bookingRejected.body: The flight slot you asked for wasn't approved.
bookingRejected.noAlternatives: There are no alternative slots to suggest right now.

bookingCancelled.subject: Your booking at {zone} has been cancelled
bookingCancelled.preview: An approved flight slot has been cancelled
bookingCancelled.heading: An approved flight slot has been cancelled
bookingCancelled.body: The flight slot below was cancelled by the authority operating the zone after it had been approved.
bookingCancelled.doNotFly: Flying at this time in this zone is no longer authorised.

bookingReminder.subject: Reminder: your flight slot at {zone}
bookingReminder.preview: Your flight slot starts within twenty-four hours
bookingReminder.heading: Your flight slot is tomorrow
bookingReminder.body: A reminder about your approved flight slot.
bookingReminder.checklist: Before take-off: check that Remote ID is broadcasting, that the aircraft carries its code sticker, and that you stay under the altitude above.

reviewQueueDigest.subject: Review queue summary
reviewQueueDigest.preview: How much is waiting right now
reviewQueueDigest.heading: Waiting for review
reviewQueueDigest.body: A periodic summary of what is waiting for review right now.
reviewQueueDigest.noPii: This summary carries counts only — no identifying detail about any operator. The details are inside the queue.
